title: Traversal controller scaffold: five assemblies, movement.json loader, capsule locomotion and jump
summary: Lay down the movement architecture from Bible §2 as separate assemblies with the IVerbProvider seam, load config/movement.json at runtime, and prove locomotion plus standing/running jump with coyote time and jump buffering on a capsule in a flat test scene. No contact verbs yet (mantle, climb, hang are M1).
scope_out: mantle, vault, hop-over, climb families, hang, slide, landing tiers (M1)
camera rules beyond a fixed follow (M1)

acceptance_tests.test: Assembly definitions GJ.Intent, GJ.TraversalQuery, GJ.AnimationSelection, GJ.MotionWarping, GJ.Procedural, and GJ.Movement.Shared (IVerbProvider, MoveClip ScriptableObject stub, MovementConfig) exist; references point only downward (an EditMode test asserting the reference graph is suggested).
MovementConfig loads unity/Assets/StreamingAssets/movement.json at startup into typed fields; a missing or extra key is a hard error with a clear message (EditMode test).
Capsule walks/jogs/runs/sprints on the flat test scene at speeds within 2 % of the constants over a 5 s run (PlayMode test).
Standing jump reaches height 1.1 A ± 5 % and distance 1.2 A ± 5 %; running jump 1.2 A / 2.4 A; coyote window 100 ms and jump buffer 120 ms verified by EditMode tests on the intent layer.
Input: floating virtual stick in the left third and a jump button on touch, plus a Bluetooth/USB gamepad via the Input System; both drive the same intent layer.
Test scene meets the SPEC §6 targets on the Owner's iPhones (a debug-overlay measurement is suggested).
No movement or camera constant is hard-coded; every number comes from MovementConfig (grep check in the PR).
